newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns citizens in Sierra Leone to stay indoors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns citizens in Sierra Leone to stay indoors.

text.p: The United States has urged its citizens in Sierra Leone to stay indoors and is prepared to evacuate them if necessary following a coup in the West African country, a White House spokesman said on Sunday.
The spokesman, Barry Toiv, also said the U.S. embassy there had been hit by twice by rocket-propelled grenades but that no one was hurt.
Soldiers in Sierra Leone ousted the civilian government Sunday and President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah flew into exile in Guinea.

Coup leaders announced a dusk-to-dawn curfew and warned Nigerian peace-keeping troops in the capitol of Freetown not to intervene. Residents reported gunfire and looting by uniformed men hours after the coup spokesman called for calm.

"We have advised U.S. citizens in Sierra Leone to stay indoors and we've made preparations, in the event that there needs to be an evacuation, but there is no evacutation going on at this point," Toiv said.
"We are obviously concerned not only about the threat to civilians but also the threat to democracy in Sierra Leone," Toiv added.

In Sierra Leone, a sergeant who identified himself as one of the coup leaders told Reuters that the army had seized parliament and the government offices at State House, as well as the radio and television.
Heavy gunfire broke out soon after 5 a.m. from the direction of State House and the military headquarters, with troops using machineguns, mortars and rocket-propelled grenades.
